gis_processing.gis_summary: Completed GIS preprocessing workflow on acquired datasets for Ratnagiri district (16.5° N to 16.9° N, 73.5° E to 74.0° E). Processed GADM district boundary vector data to generate a 5km spatial buffer and calculated total polygon surface area. Clipped 10m Sentinel-2 MSI satellite imagery composite (October 2023) and Landsat 8 OLI imagery (September 2023) to the district boundary. Computed spectral indices including Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) for vegetation health and surface water monitoring. Generated an interactive web-ready Folium/Leaflet HTML map visualizing district boundaries, buffer zones, and dataset footprints for integration into the web dashboard.

earth_observation.change_summary: Multi-temporal landscape change analysis of Ratnagiri district between 2018 and 2023 reveals stable vegetation indices combined with moderate built-up urban expansion. Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) baseline mean of 0.2895 in 2018 increased to 0.3299 in 2023, representing an absolute delta of +0.0405 (+13.99%), indicating stable vegetation health across forest and agricultural landscapes. Built-up land cover expanded from 18.72 km² in 2018 to 27.38 km² in 2023, reflecting an addition of 8.66 km² (+46.25% growth) of constructed environment. Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) across the district averages 0.1944, ranging from -0.0941 in water/coastal boundaries to 0.7884 in dense canopy zones.
detected_anomalies: Accelerated urban expansion of 8.66 km² (+46.25% increase in built-up environment) between 2018 and 2023 identified via Dynamic World LULC classification.
Localized spectral anomalies along coastal water boundaries with EVI values dropping to -0.0941.
earth_observation.event_summary: Physical transformation in Ratnagiri district (16.5° N to 16.9° N, 73.5° E to 74.0° E) over the 2018–2023 period is characterized by moderate infrastructure growth alongside resilient, stable vegetation cover. Urban and built-up land expanded by 8.66 km² (+46.25%), growing from 18.72 km² in 2018 to 27.38 km² in 2023. Regional canopy greenness experienced a slight net enhancement (+13.99% NDVI gain), demonstrating no widespread deforestation, wildfire damage, or flood-induced degradation during the observed timeframe. Overall ecological risk level is evaluated as LOW.
earth_observation.gee_interpretation: Google Earth Engine multi-spectral and multi-temporal analysis utilizing Sentinel-2 MSI (COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED) and Dynamic World 10m LULC datasets establishes that Ratnagiri district maintains a healthy ecological baseline. Sentinel-2 NDVI temporal differencing (T1: 2018 vs T2: 2023) yielded mean values rising from 0.2895 to 0.3299, classifying regional vegetation change as STABLE with zero critical deforestation alerts. Dynamic World 10m land cover classification (Label 6: Built environment) measured an increase from 18.72 km² in T1 to 27.38 km² in T2, confirming MODERATE GROWTH in urban footprint. EVI analysis confirms mean vegetation vitality at 0.1944 with maximum canopy greenness reaching 0.7884.
